facts.value: Many religions have value frameworks regarding personal behavior meant to guide adherents in determining between right and wrong.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: These include the Five Vows of Jainism, Judaism's halakha, Islam's sharia, Catholicism's canon law, Buddhism's Noble Eightfold Path, and Zoroastrianism's good thoughts, good words, and good deeds concept.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Religion and morality are not synonymous.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: While it is often assumed in Christian thought that morality is ultimately based in religion, it can also have a secular basis.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: The study of religion and morality can be contentious due to ethnocentric views on morality, failure to distinguish between in group and out group altruism, and inconsistent definitions of religiosity.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life
